The PR doesn't fix the issue. It changes BASE_RE so that an empty list no longer matches at all. That removes the bad `:` attribute, but the literal `{: }` / `{:}` text now stays in the rendered output. The issue asks for `

Title

`, `

Some paragraph

` and `

hi

`. The PR gives `

Title {: }

`, `

Some paragraph\n{:}

` and `

hi{: }

`. The new tests only check that ` :>` is missing, so they pass even though the output is wrong.

findings.title: Empty attribute list is left in the output as literal text instead of being removed
findings.evidence:
Adding `:` to the excluded first character in BASE_RE means `{: }` / `{:}` no longer match HEADER_RE, BLOCK_RE or INLINE_RE, so the treeprocessor never removes them. A probe printed `'# Title {: }' -> '

Title {: }

'`, `'Some paragraph\n{:}' -> '

Some paragraph\n{:}

'` and `'*hi*{: }' -> '

hi{: }

'`. The issue expects `

Title

`, `

Some paragraph

` and `

hi

`. A correct fix should still match and strip an empty list but add no attributes, for example by letting the captured group be empty/whitespace and having assign_attrs skip it, or by not turning a lone `:` into an attribute name.

findings.title: Tests check that ` :>` is absent instead of checking the exact expected output
findings.evidence:
`self.assertNotIn(' :>', html)` passes for the wrong output `

Title {: }

`. The tests should use `assertMarkdownRenders` with the exact output (`

Title

`, `

Some paragraph

`) and should also cover the inline case `*hi*{: }`, which the issue lists and the tests leave out. The helper `md_convert` reimplements what the TestCase base class already provides.

notes: The changelog entry has a blank line after it, so the `### Fixed` list is split up differently from the other entries. It also describes a result the code doesn't deliver: the bad attribute is gone, but the braces now appear in the text.

I wasn't allowed to run git commands to check against the base commit. Against the base code, the issue says `# Title {: }` gives `

Title

`, which contains ` :>`, so the new tests probably do fail there. They are still too weak to catch the remaining defect.
